appraisal_events.evidence: "qu'approcher suffisamment les choses et les personnes qui nous ont paru de loin belles et mystérieuses, pour nous rendre compte qu'elles sont sans mystère et sans beauté" ... "Ainsi s'était dissipée toute la gracieuse mythologie océanique que j'avais composée les premiers jours."
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator states plainly that growing familiarity dissolved the mysterious, mythic aura he had projected onto Albertine and her friends, revealing them as ordinary rather than beautiful or mysterious.

appraisal_events.evidence: "Les créatures surnaturelles qu'elles avaient été un instant pour moi mettaient encore, même à mon insu, quelque merveilleux, dans les rapports les plus banals" ... "comme si ... j'avais été en train de jouer au milieu des nymphes."
appraisal_events.explanation: Despite the preceding demystification, the narrator's closing mythological imagery (Rubens's goddesses, Hercules and Telemachus among nymphs) restores a residual enchantment to his relation with Albertine, keeping it from feeling wholly banal.

status_effects.explanation: Familiarity strips Albertine of the mysterious, mythic aura the narrator once projected onto her and her friends, reducing her locally to something ordinary and unmysterious.
The narrator's closing mythologizing image restores a residual wonder and desire to his relation with Albertine, preventing it from settling into pure banality.

ambiguities: This passage's evaluative movement concerning Albertine is largely internal to the narrator's shifting perception and belief rather than a social interaction with other characters; the demystification and later re-enchantment are framed as applying to the whole little band of girls, though only Albertine is individually named in this passage.
